subject: Materials Science
title: Solar Cells: Light to Electricity
description: A micro-lesson that makes Solar Cells: Light to Electricity usable.

hook.text: Sunlight hits a silicon wafer and electrons pop free — a p-n junction sweeps them into a wire as current.

buildup.text: Photons with energy above the band gap create electron-hole pairs — the junction's electric field separates them.

discovery.text: Silicon solar cells convert about 26% of sunlight to electricity — the theoretical limit is 33% for single junction.

twist.text: Photons below the band gap pass right through — and excess energy above it is wasted as heat.

climax.text: Multi-junction cells stack different band gaps — capturing more of the solar spectrum, reaching 47% efficiency.

punchline.text: A p-n junction in sunlight is a power plant — no moving parts, no fuel.

quiz.question: Why can't a single-junction solar cell convert all sunlight to electricity?
options: Photons below the band gap aren't absorbed and excess energy is lost as heat
Solar cells only work with infrared light
